items.t: CME Group stock: Exchange schedules London coding workshop
sum: On Wednesday, November 11, CME Group listed a London coding workshop with Google in a technology notice. The event was designed for developers and quants working with futures and options data, with participants building an analytics application during the session. CME Group described the workshop as an in-person event in London.

CME Group stock traded at 288.50 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:33 CET on Saturday, November 14. The quote provides a current market reference for investors following the US derivatives exchange from Europe.

Beyond the workshop, CME Group plans to extend implied trading functionality for selected Calendar and Butterfly spreads on CME Globex. The changes are scheduled to become effective on Sunday, November 15, for the Monday, November 16 trade date. The initiative is intended to support price discovery and order matching for products with mixed tick sizes.

The same notice sets out a new exchange-defined implied Equity Index Calendar futures spread using the AQ strategy type. The affected products include E-mini S&P 500 Equal Weight futures as well as futures linked to the Russell 1000 and Russell 2000 indexes. Customers can test the contracts in the New Release environment ahead of the launch.

Subject to regulatory review, CME Group plans to list Nikkei Basis Trade at Cash Open products on Globex from Sunday, November 15. Trading is scheduled for Wednesdays and Fridays in Japan Standard Time, beginning Wednesday, November 18, with contracts denominated in Japanese yen and US dollars.

CME Nears Uranium Storage Deal for Physical Futures Contract
sum: CME is approaching a pivotal uranium storage deal, advancing physical futures for energy investors amid rising demand and limited supply.
CME Group (NASDAQ:CME) is close to a deal to store uranium at the only commercial-scale conversion plant in the US, a step toward a futures contract based on physical yellowcake.

Bloomberg reported on Wednesday (November 11) that the exchange operator is in the process of finalizing an arrangement with ConverDyn, a 50/50 joint venture between Solstice Advanced Materials (NASDAQ:SOLS) and General Atomics, according to a person familiar with the matter.
Documents are reportedly in final legal review, with the unguaranteed expectation that the deal will close by year end.
Under the proposed terms, Solstice would manage CME’s inventories of uranium concentrate at its Metropolis Works facility in Illinois, and ConverDyn would handle the accounting.
Metropolis Works converts yellowcake into uranium hexafluoride, the form used in enrichment.

The new contract would offer an alternative to CME’s existing UxC uranium futures, which settle in cash and see little trading. It would also join a short list of products offering direct exposure to the fuel.

3 Dividend Stocks Built for a Market Priced Like It's 1999
sum: A promising new technology holds the potential to change the world. Investors enjoy multi-year gains as many stocks soar in anticipation of the tremendous opportunity. This also drives valuations to dizzying levels.

I could be talking about 1999, with the dot-com boom still going. However, 2026 fits the scenario just as well, with the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.40%) Shiller CAPE (cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings) ratio near its highest level since late 1999 and early 2000. Just substitute artificial intelligence (AI) for the internet.

We don't yet know whether the AI-driven momentum will fizzle out, as the dot-com bubble did more than a quarter-century ago. But not every stock has a nosebleed valuation today. Here are three dividend stocks built for a market priced like it's 1999.
Healthcare stocks held up much better than most when the dot-com bubble burst in 2000. I think AbbVie (ABBV +0.20%) is in a good position to do so as well, if history repeats itself.

AbbVie's shares trade below 18 times forward earnings. More importantly, the company's growth prospects appear to justify that valuation. Autoimmune disease drugs Skyrizi and Rinvoq continue to enjoy strong momentum, with sales for both soaring roughly 23% year over year in the third quarter of 2026. AbbVie's migraine therapies Qulipta and Ubrelvy delivered even more impressive growth.

The company's pipeline also looks promising. AbbVie has around 90 programs in clinical development, with two-thirds of them in mid- or late-stage testing. I'm especially keeping my eyes on ABBV-466, a combination of Skyrizi and trosunilimab that could be another blockbuster if Phase 3 testing goes as well as the Phase 2 clinical trial.

As icing on the cake, AbbVie is a member of the Dividend Kings, a group of stocks that have increased their dividends for at least 50 consecutive years. AbbVie has grown its dividend by 23% over the last five years, and it now yields 2.5%.

CME Group stock nears November 15 Globex spread upgrade
sum: CME Group is preparing a technical and product expansion on CME Globex for Sunday, November 15, with the related futures trade date beginning Monday, November 16. The exchange outlined the timetable in its CME Globex Notice dated November 2.

For selected short-term interest-rate futures, CME Group will extend implied trading to Calendar and Butterfly spreads with mixed tick legs. The company says the change is designed to support price discovery and order matching efficiency.

For Calendar spreads, off-tick implied calculations on the second leg will be rounded down for bids and up for asks to the nearest valid leg tick. Butterfly matches may produce split-price fills on the second leg. Clients can test execution, rounding and fill processing in the New Release environment before the production launch.

The same timetable introduces an exchange-defined implied equity-index Calendar futures spread using the new AQ strategy type. The affected contracts include E-mini S&P 500 Equal Weight futures, E-mini Russell 1000 futures, E-mini Russell 1000 Value futures, E-mini Russell 1000 Growth futures, E-mini Russell 2000 Value futures and E-mini Russell 2000 Growth futures.

CME Group also plans to list Nikkei Basis Trade at Cash Open products in Japanese yen and U.S. dollars, pending completion of regulatory review. Trading is scheduled for Wednesdays and Fridays in Japan Standard Time from Wednesday, November 18.

sum: CME Group closed at $315.87, a fresh one-year high that edges past its March 2 peak by 0.08%. Partner Nasdaq slipped 0.31% the same day.
CME Group closed at $315.87 on November 11, 2026, edging past the prior one-year peak set on March 2 by 0.08% and setting a new high-water mark for the stock over the past twelve months.

After dipping close to $219 mid-year, the stock recovered through the back half of the year and accelerated into this latest close. A multi-month trend carrying into a fresh annual peak reflects sustained buying interest.

A one-year high means every investor who bought CME Group over the past twelve months is now sitting on a gain. That removes a common source of overhead selling pressure and can itself become a meaningful technical signal.

Partner Nasdaq slipped 0.31% on the same day, meaning the new high was reached without a tailwind from one of CME Group's notable peers. The move looks company-specific rather than a broad market lift.

sum: CME Group (CME) is back in focus after reporting record October trading activity in interest rate and U.S. Treasury futures, as investors responded to rising Federal Reserve rate hike expectations.

The recent surge in interest rate trading has coincided with a strong run in CME Group’s shares, with a 10.17% 1‑month share price return contributing to a 14.61% year to date gain and supported by a 5‑year total shareholder return of 68.99%. This suggests momentum has been building rather than fading.

After a sharp run and record activity in its core interest rate complex, CME Group now asks you to weigh a richer share price against a still risk heavy backdrop. Does that trade off still favour new buyers?

CME Group last closed at $309.09, which sits slightly below the analyst consensus Narrative fair value of $316. According to the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St, that small gap reflects a view that most of the earnings power and risks are already captured in today’s price, with only a modest margin of upside implied.

New product introductions, such as single stock futures, compute futures on NVIDIA H100 rental costs, E mini Equity Factor futures, wind power contracts, leveraged loan index futures and a planned entry into European dairy, together with ongoing technology driven efficiencies from cloud migration and tokenization projects, give CME Group more ways to grow transaction and market data revenue while supporting high net margins.

Still, the CME Group narrative can be knocked off course if rivals gain share in key rate or energy contracts, or if regulatory outcomes around crypto and perpetual futures reduce the value investors assign to newer products.

items.t: Coinbase Falls 4%, Robinhood Slides 3% as Hot Inflation Data Drags Bitcoin Lower; Webull Declines 2%
sum: Crypto-exposed trading platforms are slipping as an inflation report that came in above forecasts sends Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) lower and revives expectations for tighter Federal Reserve policy. Coinbase Global (NASDAQ:COIN | COIN Price Prediction) stock is at $130.49 in afternoon trading, down 4%. That drop adds to a steep slide that’s left Coinbase stock down 27% over the past month.

In its Q3 2026 results, reported October 29, Coinbase posted revenue of $1.22 billion, down 35% year over year, as crypto volatility sat at multi-year lows. The company’s diluted earnings per share of $2.51 leaned on $715 million of gains on crypto assets held for investment. Adjusted net income at Coinbase, excluding those gains and other adjustments, came to $77.7 million. Management cut its full-year adjusted expense outlook, a sign that it’s leaning on cost discipline while trading stays soft.

The Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October from September, above the 0.3% estimate, according to data released November 10. Futures traders responded by pricing an 89% probability of a quarter-point Fed rate hike at the December 9 meeting, according to the FedWatch tool from CME Group (NASDAQ:CME). The Fed’s target range tops out at 4%, where it’s held since September 17.

Bitcoin trades at $73,028, down 2% over the past 24 hours. Higher-rate fears tend to weigh on speculative assets, and the 10-year Treasury yield stood at 4.88% on November 9. That background looks like the main pressure on Coinbase, since weaker crypto prices and fading risk appetite usually mean thinner trading volumes on its exchange.

Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ:HOOD) stock is at $80.67, down 3%. Over the past month, the brokerage has lost 26%, a slightly smaller slipping than Coinbase’s. Crypto trading is a meaningful swing factor for Robinhood. Options, equities, prediction markets and interest income spread its revenue across more sources, which may explain the softer drop.

Meanwhile, Webull (NASDAQ:BULL) stock is at $4.81, down 2%. As a retail brokerage built around active equity and options traders, Webull relies on trading volumes that tend to fade when risk appetite cools, though a newer crypto offering through Webull Pay adds some direct exposure to Bitcoin’s swings.

Bitcoin Cash Fell 14% This Week, Five Times Bitcoin's Drop. Where Does BCH Find Support?
sum: A CME futures headline sent Bitcoin Cash soaring in September, and the coin has since surrendered every gain and then some. Buyers defended one price level before, and traders are now watching to see whether they will show up again.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Bitcoin Cash (CRYPTO:BCH) fell 14.6% this week, while Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) fell less, down just 3.3%. BCH is at $242.73, down 5.6% in 24 hours and below its lowest close in the previous 30 days, $249.42 on November 7.

BCH has also given back the surge that followed a futures announcement from CME Group (NASDAQ:CME | CME Price Prediction). The coin jumped 30% on that news, closing at $344.97 on September 22. Now BCH is down 59.5% this year and trades 93.6% below its all-time high of $3,785.82 from December 19, 2017. So why is BCH falling so much more than Bitcoin, and where might buyers step in?

In September, CME Group announced it would launch Bitcoin Cash futures, letting traders lock in a price now to buy or sell BCH later. The contracts began trading on October 19. Investors piled in on the news, but many started selling before the launch, a pattern known as “sell the news.”

BCH closed at $306.13 on September 30 and had dropped to $270.96 by October 8, well before the futures went live. The launch brought no fresh boost either. BCH closed at $275.98 on October 18, and its late-October closes ranged from $273.42 on October 29 to $295.76 on October 27.

Futures also give large traders a regulated way to short BCH, taking a position that profits when the price falls. CME said it added the contracts because of “strong client demand for institutional-grade risk management tools,” and managing risk often means hedging against a drop. That new two-way market, combined with fading excitement after the news, may explain why BCH keeps meeting selling pressure.

CME Group stock rides record October volume into a busy week
sum: CME Group reported record derivatives activity as the week of November 1 to November 7 brought a new monthly volume high, a dividend declaration and an insider sale. The company said on November 3 that October average daily volume reached 30 million contracts, up 15 percent from October 2025, according to its CME Group release.

Interest-rate products led the October performance with average daily volume of 14.8 million contracts, while equity-index products reached 8.8 million. U.S. Treasury futures and options volume rose 48 percent year over year to 9.2 million contracts, highlighting the sensitivity of CME's core markets to changing rate expectations.

The activity report covers October rather than the trading week itself, but it gives investors a current view of the exchange operator's transaction engine. Higher volumes can support clearing and transaction revenues, although the earnings impact also depends on fee levels, product mix and market conditions.

On November 5, CME Group declared a fourth-quarter dividend of 1.30 US dollars per share. The payment is scheduled for December 30, with shareholders required to be on the register by December 11, according to Yahoo Finance, which carried the PR Newswire release.

A separate filing showed Chief Commercial Officer Julie Winkler sold 10,079 Class A shares on November 2 at a reported weighted-average price of 305.15 US dollars. She retained 21,482 shares after the transaction, according to the Form 4 filing. The filing does not establish a reason for the sale or a connection with the company's operating outlook.

CME Group stock follows record October volume of 30 million contracts
sum: CME Group reported record October trading activity on Tuesday, November 3, with average daily volume reaching 30 million contracts. The figure was 15% above October 2025, when the previous October record stood at 26.3 million contracts, according to Morningstar, which carried the company release distributed by PR Newswire.

Interest-rate average daily volume rose 28% to 14.8 million contracts. U.S. Treasury futures and options were a major driver, with average daily volume increasing 48% to 9.2 million contracts. Ten-year Treasury note futures rose 58% to 2.7 million contracts, while five-year and two-year note futures increased 50% and 51%, respectively.

Equity index average daily volume increased 15% to 8.8 million contracts. Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures climbed 74% to 2.9 million contracts, and E-mini Nasdaq-100 options increased 32% to 131,000 contracts. Energy average daily volume rose 1% to 2.7 million contracts, helped by a 221% increase in Micro WTI crude oil futures to 190,000 contracts.

International average daily volume advanced 9% to 9 million contracts. Activity in Europe, the Middle East and Africa increased 7% to 6.3 million contracts, while Asia-Pacific volume rose 15% to 2.3 million contracts.

CME Group also reported stronger activity across its related trading businesses. BrokerTec average daily notional value increased 18% to 1.127 trillion US dollars, including record US repo activity of 419.5 billion US dollars. European repo average daily notional value rose 19% to 358 billion euros, while EBS spot foreign-exchange average daily notional value increased 9% to 62.3 billion US dollars.

The October figures show that the increase was not limited to one product line. Rates, equity indexes, energy and agricultural products all set October records, while smaller contracts continued to broaden access to the exchange group's markets. Cryptocurrency average daily volume reached 145,000 contracts, representing 7.85 billion US dollars in notional value.
The real-time quote of CME Group Inc. stock showed a price of 272.25 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 13:01 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.

sum: T1 Energy Inc. TE shares are trading higher Tuesday as investors poured into technology and semiconductor stocks following Anthropic’s move toward a public listing.

Enthusiasm for artificial intelligence strengthened across global markets after Anthropic filed registration paperwork for an initial public offering. The announcement sparked buying activity in chipmakers and other AI-linked companies, helping lift T1 Energy shares. Technology stocks in Asia also advanced as traders reacted to the news.

sum: XRP advanced sharply in late August, rising from about $0.99 on August 17 to roughly $1.38 by August 31. That gain of nearly 40 percent arrived alongside a contraction in overall futures exposure, a combination that often signals traders were taking risk off rather than adding leverage into strength.
Aggregate open interest in XRP futures declined from about 2.77 billion tokens to around 2.34 billion tokens over those two weeks, a drop of 16 percent, according to CoinGlass figures.
The reduction was concentrated off the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Positions held on other venues fell by approximately 533 million tokens, or 21 percent.
Open interest on the regulated US exchange rose from 284 million tokens to about 387 million tokens, an increase of roughly 36 percent.
That lift pushed CME’s share of outstanding XRP futures from about 10 percent in mid-August to around 17 percent at month-end.
The change in market share is meaningful because many professional firms and asset managers prefer, and in some cases must use, regulated venues.

CME Grabs Bigger Slice of XRP Futures as Institutions Shift to Regulated Venues
sum: Institutional traders are increasingly routing their XRP derivatives exposure through CME Group, a shift that is quietly redrawing the competitive map for the token's futures market even as spot prices wobble.

The migration toward the Chicago-based exchange operator signals that professional desks are favoring regulated infrastructure over crypto-native venues, according to CoinDesk. While the underlying research did not pin down specific share percentages, volume figures, or open-interest numbers, the directional change in venue mix carries its own significance for how the XRP derivatives complex is evolving.

CME's growing presence in XRP futures comes at a moment when the broader crypto market is pulling back. Yet futures exposure on the exchange has continued to climb, a divergence that puts institutional positioning squarely in focus for traders trying to read how regulated derivatives behave during risk-off stretches.

Market share in XRP futures refers to the portion of total derivatives activity clearing on a given venue, not the raw size of the XRP market. A venue can gain share while overall activity stays flat, because the metric describes distribution across exchanges rather than absolute growth.

That distinction separates three commonly conflated readings: volume captures turnover over a period, open interest captures outstanding contracts at a point in time, and share measures the split between venues. The structural signal here comes from the venue mix, not from XRP price action itself.

CME has steadily built out its XRP franchise over the past year. The exchange launched Solana and XRP futures options, saw XRP futures open interest cross the $1 billion threshold, and has continued expanding its digital-asset lineup with new listings and plans for Nasdaq CME crypto index futures. A stronger XRP presence extends that push beyond bitcoin and ether into altcoin derivatives coverage.

CME operates as a regulated futures venue, and its large-trader positioning is reported through CFTC commitment data. Institutional desks typically favor exchanges that fit existing risk-management, custody, and compliance frameworks, which is one plausible reason XRP exposure would migrate there.

CHICAGO, June 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CME Group, the world's leading derivatives marketplace, today announced it will launch Single Stock futures across more than 50 of the top U.S. stocks on July 27, pending completion of all regulatory review and processes. This new offering will include 55 larger-sized and 22 Micro-sized futures contracts, providing market participants with additional flexibility to manage their equity exposure.
